title: Torsion-controlled easy algebraization triples, direction into a completion
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian, $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal, $H$ a coherent module and $N\in\operatorname{Coh}(X,J)$, as in [pqf-def-locnoeth], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $\delta:N\to\widehat H_J$ have all component kernels and cokernels annihilated by one positive power of $J$. There exist a coherent $F$, a map $a:F\to H$, and $\beta:N\simeq\widehat F_J$ satisfying $\delta=\widehat a_J\circ\beta$. The actual coherent kernel and cokernel of $a$ are annihilated by one positive power of $J$. For every other such triple $(F',a',\beta')$ whose actual map $a'$ also has kernel and cokernel annihilated by a positive power of $J$, there exists exactly one isomorphism $\gamma:F\simeq F'$ with $a'\circ\gamma=a$ and $\widehat\gamma_J\circ\beta=\beta'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('it suffices to construct (F, a, beta) Zariski locally on X'); Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian) (2); Remark 0888

proof.text: Restriction to affine opens preserves coherence, the formal-system conditions, completion, and the annihilation hypotheses. The affine coherent/formal equivalences translate delta into a map from a finite completed module to the completion of the finite module of sections of H. Remark 0888 bounds the kernel and cokernel of this limit map; ideal products and quotients are computed on affine sections.

The Noetherian ring completion is flat, the ideal is finitely generated, and reduction of the completion modulo the ideal is the original quotient ring. Completion of a finite module is naturally tensor product with the completed ring. These give the hypotheses and identifications required for formal gluing.

Formal gluing for a map with torsion kernel and cokernel constructs a module map and a compatible completed isomorphism. Its kernel and cokernel comparison isomorphisms retain a uniform annihilating exponent. The source is finite by the formal-gluing finiteness criterion, since its completion is finite and its localizations at ideal generators identify with the finite target localizations. Tilde gives the coherent triple on the affine.

For two torsion-controlled triples, their completed comparisons give an isomorphism of completed sources. Away from V(J) their maps to H are isomorphisms, giving the unique comparison on each localization at an ideal generator. These maps agree with the completed comparison on completed localizations and with each other on overlaps. Exactness of the gluing complex reconstructs the unique source map. The same construction in the reverse direction and injectivity of the gluing complex show the maps are inverses and satisfy both equations. Any isomorphism satisfying the equations has those same completed and localized maps, hence is equal.

source.place: Tag 0889(1), omitted uniqueness verification via Tag 05EK

proof.text: On overlaps, uniqueness gives the isomorphisms of triples and the cocycle equation. Glue coherent sources, maps to H, and all component comparison isomorphisms. Coherence is local. Finitely many affine opens give a uniform positive annihilating exponent for the actual coherent kernel and cokernel. Local uniqueness glues to global uniqueness.

lean.statement: theorem grothendieckExistenceEasy_torsionTriple {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData) (H : CoherentModules X) (N : CoherentFormalModule X J) (δ : N ⟶ (completion X J).obj H) (htorsion : ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ e : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2 (kernel (δ.hom.app (op e)))) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel (δ.hom.app (op e))))) : ∃ (F : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ H) (β : N ≅ (completion X J).obj F), δ = β.hom ≫ (completion X J).map a ∧ (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (kernel a.hom)) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (cokernel a.hom))) ∧ ∀ (F' : CoherentModules X) (a' : F' ⟶ H) (β' : N ≅ (completion X J).obj F'), δ = β'.hom ≫ (completion X J).map a' → (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (kernel a'.hom)) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (cokernel a'.hom))) → ∃! γ : F ≅ F', γ.hom ≫ a' = a ∧ β.hom ≫ (completion X J).map γ.hom = β'.hom
